title: TurnInput
description: Request body for POST /api/turn — the operator-submitted text, its conversation, and the timezone context the loop needs to interpret 'now' / 'today' / 'tomorrow' correctly. Per docs/005 §5 the runner is authoritative for persistence; this DTO only carries the wire fields the HTTP handler reads. The TZ fields are required so the loop never has to guess the user's frame of reference (issue #51).

conversation_id.description: Target conversation. The backend rejects the request if the caller does not own this row (docs/005 §5.2).

text.description: The user-message text submitted for this turn. Empty strings are rejected by the handler.

sent_at_utc.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the surface received the user's input. Stamped by the surface (REPL, browser composer, MCP inbound). The loop renders this into the per-turn system-prompt header so the model resolves relative time references against a known clock.

user_tz.description: IANA time zone identifier (e.g. `Europe/London`, `America/Los_Angeles`). The surface infers it: browser via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, CLI via `tzlocal()`. The loop uses it to render the user's local clock into the system-prompt header and persists it on the user message's metadata for replay correctness.
